analyzed_vuln.description: The TCP initialization path validates only that `l4_packet_len >= tcp->doff * 4`; it never enforces the TCP header's protocol minimum `doff >= 5`. The PoV supplies `doff == 2`, so `packet->payload` is incorrectly placed only 8 bytes into the TCP header and `payload_packet_len` includes header bytes. Dissector-controlled writes then populate the shared `flow->protos` union under conflicting protocol interpretations: Kerberos metadata at `flow->protos.kerberos.username` overlaps the TLS `tls_supported_versions` pointer. Because the resulting detected stack contains a TLS-family protocol, `ndpi_free_flow_data()` interprets those username bytes as a heap pointer and crashes at line 4308 while freeing `0x0606060605fe`. Cleanup is the crash site; the missing TCP data-offset validation in `ndpi_init_packet` is the root cause.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: A packet must be accepted as IPv4/TCP with at least 20 bytes of L4 data but carry a TCP data offset below 5 (the PoV uses 2). This makes bytes from inside the TCP header become application payload. In the supplied packet, source port 88 selects Kerberos and the shifted, attacker-controlled bytes satisfy the relevant Kerberos/TLS parsing heuristics; Kerberos username bytes beginning with attacker-selected nonzero values occupy the same union offset as `tls_supported_versions`, while a TLS-family protocol remains in the detected protocol stack. When the harness calls `ndpi_free_flow`, TLS cleanup attempts to free that forged pointer.

args: The reported vulnerable function is `ndpi_init_packet` in `ndpi/src/lib/ndpi_main.c` at lines 4334-4471. Is there another implementation or editable C/C++ source path for this function, and why might `ndpi/src/lib/ndpi_main.c` be classified as a fuzz harness file? Please identify the exact project source file that should be patched to enforce TCP `doff >= 5`.

I inspected `ndpi/src/lib/ndpi_main.c` and confirmed that the TCP branch at lines 4411-4417 first requires `l4_packet_len >= 20`, assigns `packet->tcp`, and then checks only `l4_packet_len >= packet->tcp->doff * 4` before deriving the application payload. The supplied PoV uses `doff == 2`, shifting payload into the TCP header and eventually forging a union pointer freed by TLS cleanup. I attempted the root-cause patch to require `packet->tcp->doff >= 5` in the same conditional, but the apply tool rejected this path with the message that it is a fuzzer harness file, even though it is under `src/lib` and the actual harness is `fuzz/fuzz_process_packet.c`. I need to determine whether there is a duplicate/upstream source path or another reason for this classification so I can modify the legitimate implementation rather than the harness.
